Can a living wall reduce stress at work?

A study of 41 adults compares living plants with a shelf in real and virtual rooms.

Our everyday environments are designed. What can this published study actually tell us about their relationship with human health and the brain?

The study

Forty-one adults completed demanding working-memory tasks in real or virtual environments, comparing a living wall with an object-filled shelf.

The findings

Heart-rate variability suggested greater physiological relaxation with the living wall, while positive emotion benefits were more evident in the real environment. Cognitive gains were not established.

What this means for architecture

Even small indoor interventions may affect stress physiology; effects should be replicated in everyday settings.

Conclusion

The evidence points to an important research question, not a universal design rule. Better controlled and longer-term studies are needed.

Serra et al. (2025)

Biophilic interventions in real and virtual environments reduce stress during cognitively demanding tasks. Scientific Reports 15, 39642
